title: Venus in transit
chineseTitle: 金星凌日：用视差丈量宇宙
intro: 文章从2004年的金星凌日回望三个多世纪的测量史：Halley 把不同地点的观测差异转化为计算日地距离的方法，远征者则在战争、天气和光学效应中艰难收集数据。最后，视差从测量太阳系尺度延伸到恒星距离，并为寻找类地行星铺路。原书中的 122 year、Healther、explores、parallax angel、重复句及其他异常均按校准来源原样保留。
overallInstructionTranslation: 建议用约20分钟完成第14—26题；这些题目基于下方阅读文章2。原书使用单数 Question 14—26，按来源保留。

sentences.english: June 2004 saw the first passage, known as a ‘transit’, of the planet Venus across the face of the Sun in 122 year.
sentences.translation: 2004年6月，人们看到了金星从太阳表面经过的现象，这种经过称为“凌日”；这是122年来的第一次。
sentences.structure: 主干是 June 2004 saw the first passage；known as 插入说明术语，of...与across...逐层限定 passage。作用：用时间与定义开启全文，并原样保留 122 year。
vocabulary: passage (B2，天文学专业词)：经过、穿越；此处指凌日过程
planet 基础词（A1/A2）：行星（天文学）；本句中的行星指代按语境确定
across the face of the Sun (B2，天文学专业表达)：越过太阳表面

sentences.english: Transits have helped shape our view of the whole Universe, as Healther Cooper and Nigel Henbest explain
sentences.translation: 正如 Healther Cooper 和 Nigel Henbest 所解释的那样，凌日现象帮助塑造了我们对整个宇宙的认识。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Transits have helped shape our view；as 从句交代解释者。作用：从单次现象提升到人类宇宙观。
vocabulary: transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
the whole Universe (B2，天文学专业词)：整个宇宙

sentences.english: On 8 June 2004, more than half the population of the world were treated to a rare astronomical event.
sentences.translation: 2004年6月8日，世界上一半以上的人口有幸看到了一次罕见的天文事件。
sentences.structure: 主干是 more than half the population were treated to an event；时间状语置前。作用：突出事件覆盖面与罕见性。
vocabulary: more than half the population (B2)：一半以上人口
be treated to (C1)：有幸享受到、看到
astronomical event (C1，天文学专业词)：天文事件

sentences.english: For over six hours, the planet Venus steadily inched its way over the surface of the Sun.
sentences.translation: 在六个多小时里，金星稳步而缓慢地从太阳表面移过。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Venus inched its way；For over six hours 给时长，steadily 描写移动方式。作用：建立凌日过程的视觉画面。
vocabulary: planet 基础词（A1/A2）：行星（天文学）；本句中的行星指代按语境确定

sentences.english: This ‘transit’ of Venus was the first since 6 December 1882.
sentences.translation: 这次金星“凌日”是自1882年12月6日以来的第一次。
sentences.structure: 主干是 This transit was the first；since 引出上次发生时间。作用：量化其稀有程度。
vocabulary: transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
the first since (B1)：自……以来第一次

sentences.english: On that occasion, the American astronomer Professor Simon Newcomb led a party to South Africa to observe the event.
sentences.translation: 上一次发生时，美国天文学家 Simon Newcomb 教授带领一支队伍前往南非观测这一事件。
sentences.structure: 主干是 astronomer led a party；On that occasion 承接前句，to observe 表目的。作用：转入历史观测。
vocabulary: astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家
lead a party (B2)：带领一支队伍

sentences.english: They were based at a girl’s school, where—it is alleged—the combined forces of three schoolmistresses outperformed the professionals with the accuracy of their observations.
sentences.translation: 他们驻扎在一所女子学校；据说，三位女教师合力作出的观测，其精确度超过了专业人员。
sentences.structure: 主干是 They were based...，where...forces outperformed professionals；插入语 it is alleged 降低断言强度。作用：以反差轶事表现观测精度。

sentences.english: For centuries, transits of Venus have drawn explores and astronomers alike to the four corners of the globe.
sentences.translation: 几个世纪以来，金星凌日同样吸引着探索者和天文学家奔赴世界各地。
sentences.structure: 主干是 transits have drawn explores and astronomers；For centuries 标时段，alike 表示两类人同样如此。作用：扩大历史与地理范围。
vocabulary: transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
explores (B2，来源异常词)：原书如此，语境指探索者
astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家；再次出现
the four corners of the globe (C1)：世界各地
globe (B2)：地球、全球；本句指世界各地

sentences.english: And you can put it all down to the extraordinary polymath Edmond Halley.
sentences.translation: 而这一切都可以归因于非凡的博学家 Edmond Halley。
sentences.structure: 主干是 you can put it all down to Halley；And 承接上文。作用：把全球行动归因于关键人物。

sentences.english: In November 1677, Halley observed a transit of the innermost planet, Mercury, from the desolate island of St Helena in the south Pacific.
sentences.translation: 1677年11月，Halley 在南太平洋荒凉的圣赫勒拿岛上观测了最内侧行星水星的一次凌日。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Halley observed a transit；多个介词短语交代时间、对象和地点。作用：说明 Halley 理论的观测起点。
vocabulary: observe (B2，科研专业词)：观测；再次出现
transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
innermost planet (C1，天文学专业词)：最内侧行星
island 基础词（A1/A2）：岛屿；此处为观测地点

sentences.english: He realized that, from different latitudes, the passage of the planet across the Sun’s disc would appear to differ.
sentences.translation: 他意识到，从不同纬度观测时，行星穿过太阳圆面的路径看起来会有所不同。
sentences.structure: 主干是 He realized that...would appear to differ；from different latitudes 前置限定观测条件。作用：引出视差。
vocabulary: appear to differ (B2)：看起来有所不同
planet 基础词（A1/A2）：行星（天文学）；本句中的行星指代按语境确定
different latitudes (B2，地理专业表达)：不同纬度

sentences.english: By timing the transit from two widely-separated locations, teams of astronomers could calculate the parallax angle—the apparent difference in position of an astronomical body due to a difference in the observer’s position.
sentences.translation: 通过在两个相距甚远的地点为凌日计时，天文学家团队可以算出视差角——也就是由于观察者位置不同而造成的天体表观位置差异。
sentences.structure: 主干是 teams could calculate the parallax angle；By timing 表手段，破折号后同位解释术语，due to 表原因。作用：给出测量机制。
vocabulary: time the transit (B2，天文学专业表达)：为凌日计时
parallax angle (C1，天文学专业词)：视差角
astronomical body (C1，天文学专业词)：天体
team of astronomers (B2，天文学专业表达)：天文学家团队

sentences.english: Calculating this angle would allow astronomers to measure what was then the ultimate goal: the distance of the Earth from the sun.
sentences.translation: 算出这个角度后，天文学家便能测量当时的终极目标：地球到太阳的距离。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Calculating this angle would allow astronomers to measure...；what 从句作 measure 的宾语，冒号揭示目标。作用：把角度转换为日地距离。
vocabulary: allow someone to measure (B1)：使某人能够测量
astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家；再次出现
distance of the Earth from the sun (B1，天文学专业表达)：地球到太阳的距离

sentences.english: This distance is known as the ‘astronomical’ or AU.
sentences.translation: 原书此处写成“astronomical”或 AU，命名结构残缺；可确定的是，这一距离用 AU（天文单位）表示。
sentences.structure: 主干是 This distance is known as...。作用：为 AU 术语命名；原书在 astronomical 后直接接 or AU，按来源保留。
vocabulary: be known as (B1)：被称为；再次出现
AU (C1，天文学专业缩写)：天文单位

sentences.english: Halley was aware that the AU was one of the most fundamental of all astronomical measurements.
sentences.translation: Halley 知道，AU 是所有天文测量中最基础的测量之一。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Halley was aware that...；that 从句说明认知内容，one of the most...突出基础地位。作用：说明 AU 的科学价值。
vocabulary: AU (C1，天文学专业缩写)：天文单位；再次出现
astronomical measurement (C1，天文学专业词)：天文测量

sentences.english: Johannes Kepler, in the early 17th century, had shown that the distances of the planets from the Sun governed their orbital speeds, which were easily measurable.
sentences.translation: 17世纪初，Johannes Kepler 已经证明，行星到太阳的距离决定其轨道速度，而轨道速度很容易测量。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Kepler had shown that distances governed speeds；插入语定位年代，which 从句补充速度可测。作用：交代已知关系。
vocabulary: orbital speed (C1，天文学专业词)：轨道速度
distance of the planets (B1，天文学专业表达)：行星距离
planet 基础词（A1/A2）：行星（天文学）；本句中的行星指代按语境确定

sentences.english: But no-one had found a way to calculate accurate distances to the planets from the earth.
sentences.translation: 但当时还没有人找到计算地球到各行星准确距离的方法。
sentences.structure: 主干是 no-one had found a way；to calculate 修饰 way。作用：与上一句形成“规律已知、距离未知”的缺口。
vocabulary: find a way to (B1)：找到方法
accurate distance (B2，科研专业表达)：准确距离
planet 基础词（A1/A2）：行星（天文学）；本句中的行星指代按语境确定

sentences.english: The goal was to measure the AU; then, knowing the orbital speeds of all the other planets round the Sun, the scale of the Solar System would fall into place.
sentences.translation: 目标是测出 AU；然后，知道其他所有行星绕太阳运行的轨道速度后，太阳系的尺度就会清晰确定。
sentences.structure: 分号连接两步：先测 AU，再依据其他轨道速度确定太阳系尺度；knowing 分词短语表示条件。作用：说明研究路线。
vocabulary: AU (C1，天文学专业缩写)：天文单位；再次出现
orbital speed (C1，天文学专业词)：轨道速度；再次出现
scale of the Solar System (C1，天文学专业词)：太阳系尺度
fall into place (C1)：变得清晰、各归其位
planet 基础词（A1/A2）：行星（天文学）；本句中的行星指代按语境确定

sentences.english: However, Halley realized that Mercury was so far away that its parallax angel would be very difficult to determine.
sentences.translation: 然而，Halley 意识到水星离得太远，其“视差 angel”会非常难以确定。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Halley realized that...would be difficult；so...that 表结果。作用：排除水星方案，并原样保留 angel。
vocabulary: parallax angel (C1，来源异常天文学词)：原书如此，语境为视差角

sentences.english: As Venus was closer to the Earth, its parallax angle would be very difficult to determine.
sentences.translation: 由于金星离地球更近，它的视差角会非常难以确定。
sentences.structure: As 从句给原因，主干是 its parallax angle would be difficult。作用：来源出现与下一句相矛盾的重复句，照录而不修正。
vocabulary: parallax angle (C1，天文学专业词)：视差角；再次出现
difficult to determine (B2)：难以确定；重复出现

sentences.english: As Venus was closer to the Earth, its parallax angle would be larger, and Halley worked out that by using Venus it would be possible to measure the Sun’s distance to 1 part in 500.
sentences.translation: 由于金星离地球更近，其视差角会更大；Halley 推算出，利用金星可以把太阳距离测量到五百分之一的精度。
sentences.structure: As 从句给原因，and 连接“角度更大”与“Halley 推算精度”；that 从句为 worked out 的内容。作用：说明选择金星的优势。
vocabulary: parallax angle (C1，天文学专业词)：视差角；再次出现
1 part in 500 (B2，测量专业表达)：五百分之一
larger (B1)：更大的；与前句 difficult 形成来源中的矛盾

sentences.english: But there was a problem: transits of Venus, unlike those of Mercury, are rare, occurring in pairs roughly eight years apart every hundred or so years.
sentences.translation: 但有一个问题：金星凌日不像水星凌日那样常见，它十分罕见，大约每百年左右成对出现，两次相隔约八年。
sentences.structure: 冒号后解释 problem；unlike 插入对比，occurring 分词短语说明出现规律。作用：转折揭示观测机会稀少。
vocabulary: transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
every hundred or so years (B2)：大约每百年
problem 基础词（A1/A2）：问题；引出金星凌日罕见这一障碍
Mercury transit (C1，天文学专业词)：水星凌日

sentences.english: Nevertheless, he accurately predicted that Venus would cross the face of the Sun in both 1761 and 1769—though he didn’t survive to see either.
sentences.translation: 尽管如此，他仍准确预言金星会在1761年和1769年两次越过太阳表面——不过他没能活到亲眼见证其中任何一次。
sentences.structure: 主干是 he predicted that...；Nevertheless 逆转困难，though 引让步。作用：以准确预言收束理论部分。
vocabulary: cross the face of the Sun (B2，天文学专业表达)：越过太阳表面

sentences.english: Inspired by Halley’s suggestion of a way to pin down the scale of the Solar System, teams of British and French astronomers set out on expeditions to places as diverse as India and Siberia.
sentences.translation: 受到 Halley 所提“确定太阳系尺度”方法的启发，英国和法国的天文学家团队出发远征，目的地从印度到西伯利亚，各不相同。
sentences.structure: Inspired by...为原因，主干是 teams set out；to pin down 修饰 way，as diverse as 强调目的地跨度。作用：从理论转向远征实践。
vocabulary: scale of the Solar System (C1，天文学专业词)：太阳系尺度；再次出现
set out on an expedition (C1)：出发远征
team of astronomers (B2，天文学专业表达)：天文学家团队；再次出现

sentences.english: But thing weren’t helped by Britain and France being at war.
sentences.translation: 但英国与法国正处于战争之中，事情因此并没有变得顺利。
sentences.structure: 主干是 thing weren’t helped；by...being at war 说明原因。作用：以战争制造实施障碍；thing 的异常原样保留。
vocabulary: be helped by (B1)：因……而变得顺利

sentences.english: The person who deserves most sympathy is the French astronomer Guillaume Le Gentil.
sentences.translation: 最值得同情的人是法国天文学家 Guillaume Le Gentil。
sentences.structure: 主干是 The person...is Le Gentil；who deserves...修饰 person。作用：聚焦个人遭遇。
vocabulary: astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家；再次出现

sentences.english: He was thwarted by the fact that the British were besieging his observation site at Pondicherry in India.
sentences.translation: 英国人当时正在围攻他位于印度本地治里的观测点，这一事实使他的计划受挫。
sentences.structure: 主干是 He was thwarted by the fact；that 从句说明事实内容，besieging 修饰英国人的行动。作用：交代首次受阻原因。
vocabulary: observation site (C1，科研专业词)：观测点
fact (B1)：事实；that从句说明具体内容

sentences.english: Feeling on a French warship crossing the Indian Ocean, Le Gentil saw a wonderful transit—but the ship’s pitching and rolling ruled out any attempt at making accurate observations.
sentences.translation: 原文句首写作“Feeling”，语义异常；其余可确定内容是：Le Gentil 在一艘横渡印度洋的法国军舰上看到了壮观的凌日，但船身的俯仰和摇摆使精确观测无法进行。
sentences.structure: 主干可确定为 Le Gentil saw a transit—but...ruled out attempt；开头 Feeling 在原书中语义与句法异常，不作推测性修正。作用：用“看见却无法测量”形成反差。
vocabulary: cross 基础词（A1/A2）：横渡；修饰法国军舰
transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
pitching and rolling (C1，航海专业词)：船体俯仰与摇摆
accurate observation (B2，科研专业词)：精确观测
see a transit (B1，天文学专业表达)：看到凌日
wonderful 基础词（A1/A2）：壮观的；描述凌日

sentences.english: Undaunted, he remained south of the equator, keeping himself busy by studying the islands of Mauritius and Madagascar before setting off to observe the next transit in the Philippines.
sentences.translation: 他没有气馁，继续留在赤道以南，先研究毛里求斯和马达加斯加群岛让自己忙起来，随后启程前往菲律宾观测下一次凌日。
sentences.structure: 主干是 he remained...；Undaunted 评述态度，keeping 分词表伴随，before setting off 标示后续。作用：突出坚持。
vocabulary: keep oneself busy (B2)：让自己忙起来
observe (B2，科研专业词)：观测；再次出现
transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
island 基础词（A1/A2）：岛屿；本句再次出现

sentences.english: Ironically after travelling nearly 50,000 kilometers, his view was clouded out at the last moment, a very dispiriting experience.
sentences.translation: 讽刺的是，他跋涉近五万公里后，视野却在最后一刻被云遮住，这是一次极其令人沮丧的经历。
sentences.structure: 主干是 his view was clouded out；after travelling 表经历，a...experience 为同位评价。作用：以反讽写第二次失败。
vocabulary: travel nearly 50,000 kilometers (B1)：跋涉近五万公里
be clouded out (C1，天文学专业表达)：因云层而无法观测
at the last moment (B1)：最后一刻

sentences.english: While the early transit timings were as precise as instruments would allow, the measurements were dogged by the ‘black drop’ effect.
sentences.translation: 虽然早期的凌日计时已达到仪器所允许的精确程度，测量仍受到“黑滴”效应的困扰。
sentences.structure: While 从句让步，主干是 measurements were dogged；as precise as...说明精度上限。作用：引出仪器无法克服的黑滴效应。
vocabulary: transit timing (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日计时
black drop effect (C1，天文学专业词)：黑滴效应
effect (B1，科研专业词)：效应；指黑滴效应
allow (B1)：允许；此处表示仪器所能达到的精度上限

sentences.english: When Venus begins to cross the Sun’s disc, it looks smeared not circular—which makes it difficult to establish timings.
sentences.translation: 金星开始越过太阳圆面时，看起来是模糊拖开的，而非圆形——这使准确确定时间变得困难。
sentences.structure: When 从句给时点，主干是 it looks smeared not circular；which 指代整个现象并说明后果。作用：具体解释计时为何困难。
vocabulary: cross the Sun’s disc (C1，天文学专业表达)：越过太阳圆面
establish timings (C1，科研专业表达)：确定计时

sentences.english: This is due to diffraction of light.
sentences.translation: 这是光的衍射造成的。
sentences.structure: 主干是 This is due to diffraction。作用：用一句因果解释黑滴现象。
vocabulary: diffraction of light (C1，物理专业词)：光的衍射

sentences.english: The second problem is that Venus exhibits a halo of light when it is seen just outside the Sun’s disc.
sentences.translation: 第二个问题是，金星刚好位于太阳圆面之外时，会呈现出一圈光晕。
sentences.structure: 主干是 problem is that Venus exhibits a halo；when 从句规定出现条件。作用：引出第二个观测障碍。
vocabulary: halo of light (C1，天文学专业词)：光晕
Sun’s disc (C1，天文学专业词)：太阳圆面；再次出现
problem 基础词（A1/A2）：问题；本句再次出现
light 基础词（A1/A2）：光（物理语境）

sentences.english: While this showed astronomers that Venus was surrounded by thick layer of gases refracting sunlight around it, both effects made it impossible to obtain accurate timings.
sentences.translation: 虽然这向天文学家表明金星周围有一层会使阳光发生折射的浓厚气体，但这两种效应都让准确计时无法实现。
sentences.structure: While 从句说明该现象提供的信息，主干是 both effects made it impossible；refracting 分词修饰 gases。作用：承认发现价值后强调计时失败。
vocabulary: thick layer of gases (B2，天文学专业表达)：浓厚气体层
refract sunlight (C1，物理专业词)：使阳光折射
make it impossible to (B2)：使……不可能
obtain accurate timings (C1，科研专业表达)：取得准确计时
astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家；再次出现
accurate timing (B2，科研专业词)：准确计时；再次出现

sentences.english: But astronomers laboured hard to analyse the results of these expeditions to observe Venus transits.
sentences.translation: 不过，天文学家仍辛勤分析这些金星凌日考察所取得的结果。
sentences.structure: 主干是 astronomers laboured to analyse；to observe 修饰 expeditions。作用：从困难转向数据整合。
vocabulary: result 基础词（A1/A2）：结果；指远征观测数据
observe (B2，科研专业词)：观测；再次出现
Venus transit (C1，天文学专业词)：金星凌日；再次出现
astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家；再次出现

sentences.english: John Franz Encke, Director of the Berlin Observatory, finally determined a value for the AU based on all these parallax measurements: 153,340,000km.
sentences.translation: 柏林天文台台长 John Franz Encke 最终根据全部视差测量结果，确定 AU 的数值为153,340,000公里。
sentences.structure: 主干是 Encke determined a value；插入语交代职务，based on 修饰 value，冒号给数值。作用：对应第18题人物与成果。
vocabulary: determine a value (B2，科研专业表达)：确定数值
AU (C1，天文学专业缩写)：天文单位；再次出现
parallax measurement (C1，天文学专业词)：视差测量
measurement (B1，科研专业词)：测量；再次出现

sentences.english: Reasonably accurate for the time, that is quite close to today’s value of methods in accuracy.
sentences.translation: 按当时的标准，这一结果相当准确，也十分接近今天的数值；原书末尾“methods in accuracy”语义异常，按来源保留。
sentences.structure: 主干是 that is close to today’s value；Reasonably accurate for the time 为前置评价。作用：评价历史结果，并原样保留异常短语 methods in accuracy。
vocabulary: methods in accuracy (C1，来源异常表达)：原书如此，语义异常，按来源保留
value (B1，科研专业词)：数值；再次出现
accuracy (B2，科研专业词)：准确性；异常短语中的词

sentences.english: The AU is a cosmic measuring rod, and the basis of how we scale the Universe today.
sentences.translation: AU 是一把宇宙测量尺，也是我们今天确定宇宙尺度的基础。
sentences.structure: and 连接两个表语：a cosmic measuring rod 与 the basis；how 从句说明 scale 的对象。作用：以比喻概括 AU 的方法论意义。
vocabulary: AU (C1，天文学专业缩写)：天文单位；再次出现
cosmic measuring rod (C1，天文学专业比喻)：宇宙测量尺
scale the Universe (C1，天文学专业表达)：确定宇宙尺度
Universe (B2，天文学专业词)：宇宙；再次出现

sentences.english: The parallax principle can be extended to measure the distances to the stars.
sentences.translation: 视差原理可以进一步用于测量恒星的距离。
sentences.structure: 主干是 principle can be extended；to measure 表用途。作用：把视差从太阳系拓展到恒星。
vocabulary: parallax principle (C1，天文学专业词)：视差原理
star 基础词（A1/A2）：恒星（天文学）

sentences.english: If we look at a star in January—when Earth is at one point in its orbit—it will seem to be in a different position from where it appears six months later.
sentences.translation: 如果我们在一月观察一颗恒星——此时地球位于其轨道上的某一点——它看起来所处的位置会与六个月后不同。
sentences.structure: If 从句设定观测，主句是 it will seem...；两个时间位置形成半年对照，when 插入解释一月位置。作用：说明恒星视差。
vocabulary: look at a star (B1)：观测恒星
at one point in its orbit (B2，天文学专业表达)：位于轨道一点
six months later 基础表达（A1/A2）：六个月后
star 基础词（A1/A2）：恒星（天文学）；本句再次出现
appear (B1)：显得、出现；后半句再次描述恒星的位置

sentences.english: Knowing the width of Earth’s orbit, the parallax shift lets astronomers calculate the distance.
sentences.translation: 知道地球轨道的宽度后，天文学家便可利用视差位移算出这段距离。
sentences.structure: Knowing...为条件，主干是 shift lets astronomers calculate。作用：收束视差计算步骤。
vocabulary: width of Earth’s orbit (C1，天文学专业表达)：地球轨道宽度
parallax shift (C1，天文学专业词)：视差位移
astronomer (B2，天文学专业词)：天文学家；再次出现

sentences.english: June 2004’s transit of Venus was thus more of an astronomical spectacle than a scientifically important event.
sentences.translation: 因此，2004年6月的金星凌日更像一场天文奇观，而不是一项具有重要科学意义的事件。
sentences.structure: 主干是 transit was more of a spectacle than an event；thus 表结论，more...than...重新评价其当代意义。作用：由科学测量转为公众奇观。
vocabulary: transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
more of A than B (C1)：与其说是B，不如说更是A
astronomical spectacle (C1，天文学专业词)：天文奇观
important event 基础表达（A1/A2）：重要事件

sentences.english: But such transits have paved the way for what might prove to be one of the most vital breakthrough in the cosmos—detecting Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars.
sentences.translation: 但这样的凌日为一项可能成为宇宙研究中最重大突破之一的发现铺平了道路——探测围绕其他恒星运行、大小与地球相当的行星。
sentences.structure: 主干是 transits have paved the way；what might prove...作 for 的宾语，破折号后动名词解释 breakthrough。作用：以系外行星发现展望未来。
vocabulary: transit (C1，天文学专业词)：凌日；再次出现
pave the way for (C1)：为……铺平道路
Earth-sized planet (C1，天文学专业词)：地球大小的行星
orbit another star (C1，天文学专业表达)：绕另一恒星运行
star 基础词（A1/A2）：恒星（天文学）；本句再次出现

deepDives.meaning: 把某个结果归因于某人或某事。本句把数百年来遍布全球的金星凌日考察归功于 Halley 的设想。
deepDives.grammar: put + 名词/代词 + down to + 原因；代词必须放在 put 与 down 之间，如 put it down to。
deepDives.context: 它把上一句宏大的历史现象迅速聚焦到一位关键人物，既口语化又有强烈归因作用。
deepDives.distinctions: attribute to 较正式；be due to 强调客观原因；credit to 常表达正面功劳；put down to 更像说话者作出的解释。
examples: The success was put down to careful observation from several locations.｜这次成功被归因于多个地点的细致观测。
She put the discrepancy down to a timing error.｜她把这项差异归因于计时误差。

deepDives.meaning: 准确确定一个原本难以固定的数值、事实或解释。本句指精确确定太阳系的尺度。
deepDives.grammar: pin down + 名词，或 pin + 名词/代词 + down；常搭配 cause、date、location、value 等。
deepDives.context: scale 本来抽象而庞大，pin down 带来“把游移对象固定住”的画面，突出测量工作的精确目标。
deepDives.distinctions: determine 正式而中性；identify 强调辨认身份；narrow down 是缩小范围；pin down 强调最终准确锁定。
examples: The team used parallax to pin down the distance to the star.｜团队利用视差准确测定那颗恒星的距离。
We need more data before we can pin down the cause of the error.｜还需要更多数据，我们才能准确确定错误原因。

deepDives.meaning: 排除某种可能性，使其不再可行。本句中军舰摇摆使精确观测根本无法进行。
deepDives.grammar: rule out + 名词/动名词；被动式 be ruled out 表示某方案已被排除。
deepDives.context: 它把“观测很困难”升级为“任何尝试都不可能”，强化 Le Gentil 看得到却测不了的挫败感。
deepDives.distinctions: exclude 偏正式，表示排除在集合之外；prevent 强调阻止发生；rule out 强调经条件判断后取消可能性。
examples: Cloud cover ruled out observing the transit that morning.｜云层使当天上午观测凌日变得不可能。
The first test did not rule out a measurement error.｜第一次测试并未排除测量误差。

instructionTranslation: 阅读文章2有 A—G 七段。
把正确字母 A—G 写在答题纸第14—17题处。
14-17.strategy: 先概括各段功能，再寻找题干中的“应用、受阻、未来发现、物理状态”同义表达；同一段可以承担一个以上信息点。

instructionTranslation: 阅读下列陈述（第18—21题）和下方人物清单。
把每条陈述与正确人物 A、B、C 或 D 配对。
把正确字母 A、B、C 或 D 写在答题纸第18—21题处。

optionTranslations.C: 纪尧姆·勒让蒂（Guillaume Le Gentil）
optionTranslations.D: 约翰·弗朗茨·恩克（Johann Franz Encke）

18-21.strategy: 人物题先建立“Halley—比较地点、Kepler—轨道速度、Le Gentil—看见但无法测量、Encke—算出 AU 数值”的对应表，再处理题干改写。

instructionTranslation: 下列陈述是否与阅读文章2中的信息一致？
NOT GIVEN：文章没有相关信息。

optionTranslations.FALES: 陈述与文章信息矛盾（原书如此拼写）

22-26.strategy: 严格区分“文章说了相反内容”和“文章没有说明”；题页把 FALSE 印成 FALES，但官方答案为 FALSE。

14.translation: 视差原理以不同方式得到应用的例子
14.logic: F段先称 AU 为宇宙测量尺，再说视差原理可扩展到恒星距离，给出两层应用。
14.distractor: B段主要定义视差并提出测量日地距离的方法；题干强调不同应用实例，F段更完整。
14.promptEnglish: examples of different ways in which the parallax principle has been applied
14.evidence: The AU is a cosmic measuring rod, and the basis of how we scale the Universe today. The parallax principle can be extended to measure the distances to the stars.

15.translation: 对一次阻止凌日观测的事件的描述
15.logic: D段中军舰俯仰摇摆 ruled out 精确观测，后来云层又挡住视野。
15.distractor: E段讲光学效应妨碍计时，不是一次历史事件。
15.promptEnglish: a description of an event which prevented a transit observation
15.evidence: Feeling on a French warship crossing the Indian Ocean, Le Gentil saw a wonderful transit—but the ship’s pitching and rolling ruled out any attempt at making accurate observations.

16.translation: 关于凌日观测可能引向未来发现的陈述
16.logic: G段用 paved the way 和 detecting Earth-sized planets 展望未来发现。
16.distractor: F段讨论已经建立的恒星距离测量方法，不是未来发现。
16.promptEnglish: a statement about potential future discoveries leading on from transit observations
16.evidence: But such transits have paved the way for what might prove to be one of the most vital breakthrough in the cosmos—detecting Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars.

17.translation: 与金星有关、早期天文仪器未能克服的物理状态描述
17.logic: E段同时描述黑滴造成的模糊形状与金星光晕，并说两者使准确计时不可能。
17.distractor: D段障碍来自战争、船体和云，而不是金星的物理状态。
17.promptEnglish: a description of physical states connected with Venus which early astronomical instruments failed to overcome
17.evidence: When Venus begins to cross the Sun’s disc, it looks smeared not circular—which makes it difficult to establish timings. The second problem is that Venus exhibits a halo of light when it is seen just outside the Sun’s disc.

18.translation: 他根据对金星的观测，以相当高的准确度算出了太阳到地球的距离。
18.logic: F段 Encke based on all these parallax measurements 得出153,340,000km，对应 D。
18.distractor: Halley 提出方法并预测凌日，但没有给出该数值；Kepler 研究轨道速度；Le Gentil 未能测量。
18.promptEnglish: He calculated the distance of the Sun from the Earth based one observations of Venus with a fair degree of accuracy.
18.evidence: John Franz Encke, Director of the Berlin Observatory, finally determined a value for the AU based on all these parallax measurements: 153,340,000km.

19.translation: 他明白，可以通过比较对一次凌日的观测来算出日地距离。
19.logic: B段 Halley 指出在两个相距甚远的地点计时可算视差角，对应 A。
19.distractor: Encke 是后来汇总测量得到数值，不是最先理解比较观测方法的人。
19.promptEnglish: He understood that the distance of the Sun from the Earth could be worked out by comparing observations of a transit.
19.evidence: By timing the transit from two widely-separated locations, teams of astronomers could calculate the parallax angle—the apparent difference in position of an astronomical body due to a difference in the observer’s position.

20.translation: 他意识到，行星绕太阳一周所需时间取决于它与太阳的距离。
20.logic: C段明确说 Kepler 证明距离 governed orbital speeds，对应 B。
20.distractor: Halley 利用这项既有规律设计 AU 测量，但该发现归于 Kepler。
20.promptEnglish: He realized that the time taken by a planet to go round the Sun depends one its distance from the Sun.
20.evidence: Johannes Kepler, in the early 17th century, had shown that the distances of the planets from the Sun governed their orbital speeds, which were easily measurable.

21.translation: 他亲眼看见一次金星凌日，却无法进行任何计算。
21.logic: D段 Le Gentil 在军舰上看见凌日，但船体运动排除了精确观测，对应 C。
21.distractor: A Halley 提出比较不同地点观测的方法；B Kepler 说明轨道速度与距离的关系；D Encke 根据视差计算 AU，三者都不符合“看见凌日却无法测量”。
21.promptEnglish: He witnessed a Venus transit but was unable to make any calculations.
21.evidence: Feeling on a French warship crossing the Indian Ocean, Le Gentil saw a wonderful transit—but the ship’s pitching and rolling ruled out any attempt at making accurate observations.

22.translation: Halley 观测过一次金星凌日。
22.logic: 文章说 Halley 观测的是水星凌日，且他在预言的两次金星凌日前已经去世，因此为 FALSE。
22.distractor: 不能把 Mercury transit 偷换成 Venus transit；predicted 也不等于 observed。
22.promptEnglish: Halley observed one transit of the Planet Venus.
22.evidence: In November 1677, Halley observed a transit of the innermost planet, Mercury, from the desolate island of St Helena in the south Pacific. Nevertheless, he accurately predicted that Venus would cross the face of the Sun in both 1761 and 1769—though he didn’t survive to see either.

23.translation: Le Gentil 成功观测了第二次金星凌日。
23.logic: 第一次他看见却无法测量；下一次在最后一刻被云遮住，所以没有成功观测第二次，为 FALSE。
23.distractor: remained south...to observe 只表示计划，不能推断成功。
23.promptEnglish: Le Gentil managed to observe a second Venus transit.
23.evidence: Feeling on a French warship crossing the Indian Ocean, Le Gentil saw a wonderful transit—but the ship’s pitching and rolling ruled out any attempt at making accurate observations. Ironically after travelling nearly 50,000 kilometers, his view was clouded out at the last moment, a very dispiriting experience.

24.translation: 金星开始从太阳前方经过时，其形状看起来会变形。
24.logic: E段明确说它 looks smeared not circular，因此为 TRUE。
24.distractor: 题干 distorted 是 smeared not circular 的同义改写，不要求原词完全相同。
24.promptEnglish: The shape of Venus appears distorted when it starts to pass in front of the Sun
24.evidence: When Venus begins to cross the Sun’s disc, it looks smeared not circular—which makes it difficult to establish timings.

25.translation: 地球上的天文学家怀疑金星的大气有毒。
25.logic: 文章只由光晕推知金星被一层浓厚气体包围，没有提供毒性信息，因此为 NOT GIVEN。
25.distractor: 不能从 gases 或 atmosphere 自行推断 toxic，也不是 FALSE，因为原文没有说“无毒”。
25.promptEnglish: Earth astronomers suspected that the atmosphere on Venus was toxic.
25.evidence: While this showed astronomers that Venus was surrounded by thick layer of gases refracting sunlight around it, both effects made it impossible to obtain accurate timings.
25.location: Passage 2, paragraph E, physical page 43 (atmosphere mentioned; toxicity not stated)

26.translation: 视差原理使天文学家能够算出遥远恒星距地球有多远。
26.logic: F段明确说视差原理可扩展用于测量恒星距离，并解释半年位置差，故为 TRUE。
26.distractor: 尽管原文后句省略 from the Earth，地球轨道基线已明确说明参照点。
26.promptEnglish: The parallax principle allows astronomers to work out how far away distant stars are from the Earth.
26.evidence: The parallax principle can be extended to measure the distances to the stars.
